item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like this idea, but I also feel it's vastly under utilized. I would like to see more instances of testing, and whether or not the animate objects become fully sapient if exposed for long enough. Perhaps exposure to a white-collar D for a long period of time, then interviewing the resulting 692-X (give it gloves, pen and paper, and keep it in a locked cell). If viable, these copies could be an extremely cheap method of "cloning" low level lab assistants and test subjects able to interact with SCP unapproachable by living testers.

Also, I don't see the issue with 692-1 being kept as a pet. There are several other instances of safe SCPs being kept as pets (Pterry (346), the origami crane (368), Josie (529), etc.). There's no evidence that these entities are dangerous unless imprinted upon something dangerous.
